title: Blues singers and Ma Rainey's Countin' the Blues
summary: Gleason introduces a Ma Rainey record; Armstrong says singers like Bessie, Mamie and Clara Smith played theaters rather than Oliver's Lincoln Gardens.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: Was there any vocalist with the band? No, no vocalist. But then you made records shortly after that. After that, yeah. With vocalists, with Bessie Smith. Yeah. But that was when I went with Fletch Henderson, after I left Joe, 1924. I thought we could play one of the records by Ma Rainey that you played on, as an example of the kind of blues of that period and the blues singers and the way in which you worked with them. This one is called Countin' the Blues by Ma Rainey with the accompaniment by Louis Armstrong, Fletcher Henderson, group from the Fletcher Henderson Band. Ma Rainey is Countin' the Blues. Ma Rainey is Countin' the Blues.
